recognize_zh: 中央有一顆明顯大於周圍血小板、接近紅血球大小的顆粒狀紫色物體，中心顆粒集中、邊緣淡而有突起，是大型／巨大血小板（giant platelet）。
features: Central platelet markedly larger than surrounding platelets, approaching the diameter of adjacent red cells
Central concentration of purple granules (granulomere) with a paler, finely fimbriated peripheral hyalomere
Several other scattered platelets, some also enlarged with visible granules
An ovoid pale lilac structure at the top of the field, possibly another large platelet seen en face
Background normocytic red cells with occasional target-like forms; no leukocytes in field
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows normocytic red cells with occasional target-like forms and scattered platelets of variable size. In the center is a platelet approaching the size of an adjacent red cell, with centrally clustered purple granules and a pale, irregular peripheral rim. Several other platelets are also larger than normal. No platelet clumps or leukocytes are seen in this field. Findings are consistent with large to giant platelets; correlation with platelet count and clinical context (increased turnover, myeloid neoplasm or inherited macrothrombocytopenia) is needed.

ddx.vs: A lymphocyte has a dense round nucleus with a rim of blue cytoplasm, whereas a platelet is anucleate with granular purple center and pale hyalomere.
Overlap produces a normal-sized platelet superimposed on a red cell in the same focal plane, not a free-standing enlarged platelet.
Megakaryocyte nuclei or nuclear fragments show dense chromatin, which is absent in this anucleate platelet.
